issues.description: The problem statement / UML declares numberOfTutors as type int, but the solution implementation declares the attribute numberOfTutors as type short. This inconsistency in the attribute type can confuse students about the expected type and lead to mismatches in constructor parameters, setters, or tests that expect an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent with the UML/problem statement. Change the solution's numberOfTutors field from short to int (and adjust any related setter/getter signatures accordingly), or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to specify short if that was intended. Preferably use int to match the UML and avoid truncation issues.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a constructor that initializes all attributes in the order and types specified by the UML (numberOfTutors is declared as int), but the solution's constructor accepts a short for numberOfTutors. This parameter type mismatch between specification and solution may mislead students when implementing the constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter type with the UML/specification. Change the constructor parameter for numberOfTutors in the solution to int (and set the field to int), or update the UML/spec to expect short if that was intended. Prefer using int for consistency with the rest of the integer attributes.
